skill.name: markitdown
skill.description: Convert PDF, Office, web, image, audio, data, archive, and EPUB files to Markdown using Microsoft MarkItDown.
skill.summary: Convert many file formats into clean, LLM-ready Markdown with optional AI image descriptions.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples, Markdown code fences, placeholder API keys, or user-directed output writes. Confirmed risks remain where the skill instructs sudo package installation, writes API keys into shell profiles, displays an API key, and sends converted content to OpenRouter. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Keep sudo package installation as manual prerequisite guidance and require explicit user approval before any elevated command runs.

remediation.issue: Persistent API key storage in shell profiles
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell profile append commands with session-scoped environment variables, a secrets manager, or redacted setup instructions.
Replace direct API key echo commands with a redacted presence check that never prints the full value.
Add a clear privacy warning before OpenRouter conversion and keep local-only conversion as the default path.
Disable plugins by default and warn users to enable only trusted MarkItDown plugins.

content.user_title: Convert Files to Markdown with MarkItDown
content.value_statement: Teams often need clean Markdown from PDFs, Office files, images, audio, and web content. This skill provides MarkItDown guidance, scripts, and examples for repeatable conversion workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains MarkItDown installation for full or format-specific dependencies.
Shows conversion for PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP, EPUB, audio, images, and YouTube URLs.
Includes batch conversion scripts for directories, recursive searches, and selected file extensions.
Provides a literature conversion script that organizes papers and creates Markdown indexes.
Documents optional OpenRouter use for AI-generated image and slide descriptions.
limitations: The skill requires Python and the MarkItDown package to run conversions.
OCR, audio transcription, YouTube transcripts, and Azure processing need optional dependencies or accounts.
AI image descriptions send content to OpenRouter and require a user-provided API key.
Conversion quality depends on the source file structure and available extraction libraries.

use_cases.title: Prepare Research Papers
use_cases.description: Convert PDFs into Markdown notes, then organize them by year for review workflows.

use_cases.title: Create LLM-Ready Documents
use_cases.description: Turn Office files, web pages, and data files into text that language models can process efficiently.

use_cases.title: Batch Process Document Sets
use_cases.description: Convert folders of mixed documents into a consistent Markdown output directory.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use MarkItDown to convert this document to Markdown. Keep headings, tables, and metadata readable.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Convert a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert all PDFs and Office files in this folder to Markdown. Save outputs in a separate directory and report failures.

prompt_templates.title: Add AI Image Descriptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this presentation with AI image descriptions through OpenRouter. Use a scientific prompt and note any privacy concerns first.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Literature Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a literature conversion workflow for these PDFs. Extract metadata, organize by year, and generate a Markdown index.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks to convert a folder of papers for a literature review.
output: Markdown files are created for each paper.
An index groups papers by year and links to each converted file.
The summary reports successful and failed conversions.

output_examples.input: A writer asks to convert a slide deck with figures into Markdown.
output: Slide text is converted into Markdown sections.
Figures receive AI-generated descriptions when OpenRouter is configured.
The output includes source file metadata and the selected model name.

output_examples.input: An analyst asks to process spreadsheets and web pages for LLM review.
output: Tables are represented in Markdown form.
HTML content is cleaned into readable text.
The final files are ready for search, summarization, or review.

best_practices: Use a virtual environment and install only the format dependencies you need.
Review sensitive files before using OpenRouter or other remote services.
Write converted files to a dedicated output directory to avoid overwrites.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into examples, logs, or shared notes.
Do not enable third-party plugins unless their source and behavior are trusted.
Do not run elevated installation commands through an automated agent.

faq.answer: It covers common document, office, image, audio, web, data, archive, EPUB, and YouTube transcript workflows supported by MarkItDown.

faq.question: Does it work without external AI services?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic MarkItDown conversion is local, but AI image descriptions require OpenRouter or another configured LLM service.

faq.question: Can it process many files at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The included batch script converts folders, supports recursive search, and filters by file extension.

faq.question: Is OCR included by default?
faq.answer: OCR depends on optional packages and system tools such as Tesseract.

faq.question: Can it organize academic papers?
faq.answer: Yes. The literature script converts PDFs, extracts filename metadata, optionally groups by year, and creates an index.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing outputs?
faq.answer: Review converted Markdown for sensitive data, extraction errors, and third-party AI descriptions that may need verification.
